---
title: "Methods showcase"
description: "A worked example of the kind of analysis I do: a multilevel model for simulated EMA data, with a simulation-based power check."
---

Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) yields many repeated prompts nested within participants. Below I simulate a small EMA study, fit a random-intercept, random-slope model with **lme4**, and estimate power by simulation. The data are simulated; no real participant data are used.

## Simulate EMA data

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(lme4)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(2026)

sim_ema <- function(n_id = 60, n_prompts = 42, b_stress = 0.35) {
  ids <- tibble(id = factor(seq_len(n_id)),
                u0 = rnorm(n_id, 0, 0.8),      # person-level intercept
                u1 = rnorm(n_id, 0, 0.15))     # person-level slope
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids$id, prompt = seq_len(n_prompts)) |>
    left_join(ids, by = "id") |>
    mutate(stress   = rnorm(n()),               # within-person (centered) stress
           craving  = 2 + u0 + (b_stress + u1) * stress + rnorm(n(), 0, 1),
           answered = rbinom(n(), 1, 0.78) == 1) |>   # ~78% EMA compliance
    filter(answered)
}

ema <- sim_ema()
glimpse(ema)
```

## Fit a multilevel model

```{r}
#| label: model
fit <- lmer(craving ~ stress + (1 + stress | id), data = ema)
summary(fit)$coefficients |> round(3)
VarCorr(fit)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-slopes
#| fig-cap: "Person-specific stress–craving slopes (random effects) around the fixed effect"
pred <- ema |> mutate(fitted = fitted(fit))
ggplot(pred, aes(stress, fitted, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = .25, colour = "#1f4e79") +
  geom_abline(intercept = fixef(fit)[1], slope = fixef(fit)[2], linewidth = 1.2, colour = "#c0392b") +
  labs(x = "Momentary stress (within-person, SD units)", y = "Predicted craving") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## Simulation-based power

```{r}
#| label: power
power_at <- function(n_id, reps = 100, b = 0.15) {
  hits <- replicate(reps, {
    d <- sim_ema(n_id = n_id, b_stress = b)
    m <- suppressMessages(lmer(craving ~ stress + (1 + stress | id), data = d,
                               control = lmerControl(check.conv.singular = "ignore")))
    abs(coef(summary(m))["stress", "t value"]) > 1.96
  })
  mean(hits)
}
power_tbl <- tibble(n_id = c(20, 40, 60, 80)) |>
  mutate(power = vapply(n_id, power_at, numeric(1)))
knitr::kable(power_tbl, digits = 2, col.names = c("Participants", "Power (β = 0.15)"))
```

Because `freeze: auto` is set, this simulation runs only when the page changes locally, and CI reuses the cached results.
